policy_title: Make St George's and St David's Day public holidays
stated: Reform UK will make St George’s and St David’s Day public holidays, stating that English national identity should be officially promoted and celebrated.

source.quote: Make St George’s and St David’s Day a Public Holiday English national identity should be officially promoted and celebrated, not ignored or banned.

bearing_set.reason: Adding two bank holidays directly affects working conditions — entitling most employees to extra paid leave while imposing real costs on employers, particularly SMEs, creating a non-negligible trade-off in job quality and labour economics.

The policy explicitly aims to promote English and Welsh national identity through official celebration; its effect on social trust, shared belonging, and inter-group relations earns a real — if contested in direction — verdict on cohesion.

Each additional bank holiday measurably reduces working days, with a non-negligible near-term productivity and output cost (estimated £2–3bn per holiday by bodies such as CEBR), partially offset by leisure/hospitality gains — a genuine, evidence-assessable effect on living standards.

membership_note: The policy bears primarily on community belonging (O15) and aggregate prosperity/living standards (O13) via the productivity cost of lost working days. Effects on O4 (workers gain extra paid leave) are real but marginal given the policy changes no employment right beyond adding two holidays. O9 (equal treatment) and O11 (tax) are not materially engaged.
